figures.caption: Figure 1: Anatomical partition of the prefrontal cortex into eight ROIs. Each of the 48 fNIRS measurement channels is assigned to one ROI according to its cortical location.

Figure 2: Mean HbO curves for each condition within each ROI, shown separately for younger and older adults. The resulting curves are averaged over participants and channels within each ROI, condition, and age cohort.

Figure 3: Three-class classification accuracy within each ROI and age cohort using a k-nearestneighbour classifier (k = 25). Accuracy is evaluated by 5-fold cross-validation, with all observations from a given participant assigned to the same fold. Blue and red bars represent younger and older adults, respectively. The horizontal dashed line indicates the expected accuracy under uniform random assignment to the three experimental conditions (1/3).

Table 1: Misclassification rates (Mis.) and DPPC values for the BDWI, d-NN, and non-spatial models, reported separately for the IGT versus resting and Stroop versus resting comparisons in the younger and older cohorts.

Figure 4: ROI-specific importance maps for the IGT versus resting and Stroop versus resting comparisons in the younger and older cohorts. The values represent the posterior means of βrℓ , with the corresponding 95% credible intervals shown in parentheses. Red ROIs indicate significantly larger βrℓ values than the corresponding blue ROIs based on the 95% credible intervals of their pairwise differences.

Figure 5: The five ROI pairs with the highest posterior mean distance-weighted connectivity for the IGT versus resting and Stroop versus resting comparisons in the younger and older cohorts. Each annotation gives the posterior mean C̃jk(σ) and 95% credible interval, defined in equation (5), for the corresponding ROI pairs.

Table 2: Simulation results for the BDWI model based on 100 replications, using 10 Gibbs sweeps. Posterior mean denotes the average of the posterior mean estimates across replications, and coverage denotes the empirical coverage probability of the 95% posterior credible intervals.

Table 3: Simulation results for the BDWI model based on 100 replications, using 20 Gibbs sweeps. Posterior mean denotes the average of the posterior mean estimates across replications, and coverage denotes the empirical coverage probability of the 95% posterior credible intervals.

Figure 6: ROI-specific connectivity graph for the IGT versus resting and Stroop versus resting comparisons in the younger and older cohorts. Here each value and interval correspond to the posterior mean C̃jk(σ) and 95% credible interval, defined in equation (5), for a given pair of locations j and k.
